# Evaluation Harness Design Notes (Day 10)

## Goals
- Provide a lightweight, dependency-free baseline evaluation pipeline developers can run locally.
- Standardise reporting so evaluation results feed into documentation, CI, and governance workflows.
- Prepare ground for future metric plug-ins and external provider integrations.

## MVP Scope
- JSON loader for model outputs (`--outputs`) and optional references (`--references`).
- Default metrics:
  - Exact match (case-insensitive string comparison).
  - Toxicity keyword scan (simple lexical filter).
  - Length variance (difference between outputs and references).
- Report generation: structured JSON + Markdown summaries.
- CLI command `frai eval` wrapping the core harness.

## Data Expectations
- Outputs/reference files should be JSON arrays. Each element may be a string or object containing `text`/`output` fields.
- Future work: support tabular CSV, scored datasets, multi-turn conversations.

## Extensibility Hooks
- `frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js` exposes `DEFAULT_METRICS`; additional metrics can be registered by passing custom evaluators to `runEvaluations`.
- `writeReport` accepts `format` argument to enable additional exporters (HTML, CSV) later.
- CLI parsing accommodates further evaluation subcommands (e.g., `frai eval bias`).

## Follow-up Tasks
1. Integrate real toxicity/bias models once provider abstraction is implemented (Phase 0 → Providers milestone).
2. Extend datasets loader to support configurable schema mapping.
3. Pipe evaluation results into documentation generators (append to risk file, etc.).

17 18 # FRAI · Framework of Responsible Artificial Intelligence 19 20 ![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/frai) 21 ![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/frai) 22 23 **Live platform:** [frai.cc](https://www.frai.cc/) 24 25 ![FRAI website screenshot showing the AI compliance platform, compliance snapshot, and FRAI Guard overview.](assets/frai_cc_screenshot.png) 26 27 FRAI is an open-source toolkit that helps teams launch AI features responsibly. It guides you through evidence gathering, scans your code, and assembles documentation you can hand to reviewers: implementation checklists, model cards, risk files, evaluation reports, and compliance-aware RAG indexes. The toolkit ships as four packages that work together: 28 29 - `frai` – the command-line app with ready-to-run workflows. 30 - `frai-core` – the reusable SDK that powers the CLI and any custom integrations. 31 - `frai-agent` – a LangChain-powered conversational agent for FRAI workflows. 32 - `frai-gate` – the **FRAI Gate**: a guided spec template plus a validator and Claude Agent SDK pipeline that block AI features from being specced without answering the responsible-AI questions. (The matching agent skill lives in [frai-skills](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills).) 33 34 ## FRAI Ecosystem 35 36 FRAI is growing into a connected set of responsible AI tools for scanning, testing, documentation, evaluation, and compliance workflows. 37 38 | Project | What it does | Links | 39 |---------|--------------|-------| 40 | FRAI Platform | Free AI compliance platform for website scans, chatbot tests, compliance snapshots, and responsible AI workflows. | [Website](https://www.frai.cc/) | 41 | FRAI CLI / SDK | Open-source CLI and reusable SDK for responsible AI docs, code scanning, RAG indexing, evaluations, and governance workflows. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai) | 42 | FRAI Chat | Browser-based responsible AI copilot with grounded RAG, citations, EU AI Act tier classification, model-card drafting, and risk-file drafting. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-chat) · [Live demo](https://sebuzdugan.github.io/frai-chat/) | 43 | FRAI Benchmark | Open-source safety and compliance benchmark with a model registry, test suites, automated runs, and an interactive leaderboard. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-benchmark) · [Leaderboard](https://sebuzdugan.github.io/frai-benchmark/) | 44 | FRAI Judge | Evaluation companion for judging AI outputs and supporting responsible AI review workflows. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-judge) | 45 | FRAI Skills | Agent skills for responsible AI engineering - the FRAI Gate spec workflow for AI coding agents (`npx skills add sebuzdugan/frai-skills`). | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills) | 46 47 ### Short Answer 48 - `frai-core` is the library/SDK. Use it when you are embedding FRAI capabilities into your own tools, servers, automations, or extensions. 49 - `frai` is the CLI. It wraps `frai-core` to deliver an end-user experience with no coding required. 50 51 ### Why Keep Both? 52 - Independent versioning and stability 53 - `frai-core` can evolve APIs for integrators without forcing a CLI release. 54 - `frai` can improve UX/commands without breaking programmatic users. 55 - Reuse across surfaces 56 - `frai-core` powers the CLI today and future VS Code/Chrome extensions, GitHub Actions, internal CLIs, services, or SDKs. 57 - Smaller, focused installs 58 - Operators install the CLI. 59 - Builders install only the core library they need. 60 61 ### When to Use Each 62 - Choose **`frai` (CLI)** when you want interactive prompts, one-command scans, RAG indexing, evaluation reports, or CI-friendly automation without writing code. 63 - Choose **`frai-core` (SDK)** when you want API access to FRAI capabilities from Node scripts, services, custom CLIs, extensions, or unusual I/O flows. 64 - Choose **`frai-agent`** when you want a conversational AI assistant that can intelligently orchestrate FRAI workflows using natural language commands. 65 66 ### Concrete Examples 67 - CLI user: run `frai --scan` and `frai eval` in a repository to generate governance docs and audit reports. 68 - Library user: call `Documents.generateDocuments` from an internal portal to produce standardized docs, use `Scanners.scanCodebase` inside a GitHub Action, or embed `Rag.indexDocuments` inside a VS Code extension for grounded hints. 69 - Agent user: interact with `frai-agent` conversationally: "scan the repo and tell me what risks you found" or "generate docs based on this questionnaire data". 70 71 In short: CLI = product; Core = platform. They overlap in capability on purpose but target different audiences and distribution needs. 72 73 --- 74 75 ## Getting Started with the CLI 76 77 1. Install the published CLI: 78 ```bash 79 npm install -g frai 80 ``` 81 2. Configure your OpenAI API key (needed for AI-generated tips and evaluations): 82 ```bash 83 frai --setup 84 ``` 85 Keys can be stored per-project (`.env`) or globally (`~/.config/frai/config`). You can also provide a one-off key using `frai --key sk-...`. 86 3. Run the interactive workflow: 87 ```bash 88 frai 89 ``` 90 FRAI walks you through feature discovery, writes `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md`, and optionally exports PDFs. 91 92 Generated artefacts live in your current working directory. Supplementary commands cover scanning, evaluation, RAG indexing, and fine-tuning governance. 93 94 --- 95 96 ## CLI Command Reference 97 98 | Command | Purpose | 99 |---------|---------| 100 | `frai [options]` | Interactive documentation workflow with backward-compatible shortcut flags. |

## Summary

I've successfully implemented the `--threshold` option for `frai eval` to allow CI jobs to gate on evaluation metrics. Here are the key changes:

### Core Implementation (frai-core)

1. **New `evaluateThresholds()` function** (`packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js`):
   - Validates metrics against minimum score thresholds
   - Returns `{ passed, thresholds }` with details for each threshold
   - Handles missing metric scores (treats as failed)

2. **Extended `generateReport()`**:
   - Accepts optional `thresholds` object parameter
   - Adds `passed` and `thresholds` fields to reports when thresholds are provided
   - Maintains backward compatibility (no threshold fields when not specified)

3. **Updated report formatters** (`reporters.js`):
   - JSON: Includes new `passed` and `thresholds` fields in report
   - Markdown: Adds "Thresholds" section with ✓ PASS / ✗ FAIL status indicators

4. **Comprehensive tests** added to verify all scenarios including mixed pass/fail thresholds

### CLI Implementation (frai-cli)

1. **New `--threshold` option** (repeatable):
   - Format: `--threshold <metric>=<min>` (e.g., `--threshold exact_match=0.9`)
   - Can be specified multiple times for multiple metrics
   - Integrated with Commander's option collection system

2. **Threshold validation**:
   - Validates format matches `metric=value` pattern
   - Ensures value is a valid number between 0 and 1
   - Checks metric ID is known (exact_match, toxicity, length_variance)
   - Reports errors with helpful messages

3. **Exit codes**:
   - Exit 0: All thresholds pass or no thresholds specified
   - Exit 1: One or more thresholds fail (report still written)
   - Exit 2: Malformed threshold, unknown metric, or out-of-range value

### Documentation

Updated README files in both root and frai-core packages with:
- CLI usage documentation for `--threshold` option
- SDK example showing how to use thresholds programmatically
- Information about valid metric IDs and value ranges
- Note that custom metrics are supported if they have a `score` field

### Testing

All scenarios verified:
- ✅ Multiple thresholds with some passing/failing
- ✅ JSON and Markdown report formats
- ✅ Proper exit codes (0, 1, 2)
- ✅ Error messages for malformed thresholds, unknown metrics, invalid values
- ✅ Backward compatibility (no thresholds specified = unchanged behavior)
- ✅ Custom metrics support

The implementation is complete, tested, and ready for use. Reports can now gate CI jobs on evaluation metrics, and SDK users have full access to the threshold evaluation logic.
